full_sentence: My brother has already finished his breakfast.

options.why_wrong: The present continuous does not follow 'has already'. The present perfect needs a past participle such as 'finished'.
'Yesterday' is a finished time and cannot be used with the present perfect 'has already'.
The future 'will' does not fit 'has already', which describes an action completed before now.

explanation: 'Already' signals that an action was completed before the present moment. After 'has already', we need the past participle of the verb to show a completed action linked to now. Learners whose first language marks past actions differently may need extra practice with this structure.
